provenance.basis: Independent learning objectives; no source question paraphrasing
provenance.verification: Automated grading, domain and numerical checks; see local audit report

grading_policy: One point for the final short answer or selected option. Does not assess proof or written reasoning. Numeric tolerance is absolute 0.000001; decimals to at least six places or a number/fraction. No general expression evaluation.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: check 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(x^2+x-20=0\), enter the positive root.
questions.hint_html: Find two integers with product -20 and sum 1.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(3x^2-8x-3=0\), enter the negative root.
questions.hint_html: Try factors of 3x squared and -3.

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(x(x-6)=0\). Which is the complete real solution set?
questions.hint_html: A product is zero when either factor is zero.
questions.solution_html: Dividing by \(x\) would lose \(x=0\). Both \(0\) and \(6\) satisfy the equation.
questions.focus: do not divide away a root

questions.title: Factorisation and valid roots: check 4
questions.hint_html: Check the original denominator before cancelling.
questions.solution_html: \(x\ne3\). The numerator is zero at \(\pm3\), but only \(-3\) is allowed.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Write \(x^2-10x+8=(x-p)^2+q\), where \(p>0\). Enter \(p\).
questions.hint_html: Halve the coefficient of x.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum value of \(2x^2+12x+23\).
questions.hint_html: Factor 2 from the quadratic and linear terms.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the maximum value of \(-3x^2+12x-7\).
questions.hint_html: A negative square is at most zero.

questions.title: Completing the square and range: check 4
questions.prompt_html: How many real roots does \(4(x-2)^2+7=6\) have?
questions.hint_html: A real square cannot be negative.
questions.solution_html: The equation requires \((x-2)^2=-1/4\), impossible over the reals.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the discriminant of \(2x^2-5x+4\).
questions.hint_html: Use b squared minus 4ac.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For which value of \(k\) does \(x^2+8x+k=0\) have a repeated root?
questions.hint_html: Set the discriminant to zero.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: check 3
questions.prompt_html: How many distinct real solutions does \(x^4-13x^2+36=0\) have?
questions.hint_html: Set u equal to x squared, then return to x.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(x-6\sqrt{x}+8=0\) over the reals.
questions.hint_html: Set u = square root of x with u non-negative.

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: check 1
questions.hint_html: Test a point between the roots.
questions.solution_html: The upward quadratic is negative strictly between its roots: \(-2<x<5\).

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(x^2-9\ge0\).
questions.hint_html: The boundary roots are included.
questions.solution_html: The product \((x-3)(x+3)\) is non-negative outside the roots, including both.

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: check 3
questions.prompt_html: How many integers satisfy \(x^2-3x-10<0\)?
questions.hint_html: Factor, then count integers strictly between the roots.

questions.title: Quadratic inequalities and integer constraints: check 4
questions.hint_html: The negative of a square is never positive.
questions.solution_html: \(-(x-1)^2\le0\) for all real \(x\), so there are no solutions.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: check 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x+2\) and \(y=x^2\), enter the larger x-coordinate of intersection.
questions.hint_html: Substitute the linear y expression into the quadratic.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=2x+3\) and \(x^2+y^2=9\), one intersection is \((0,3)\). Enter the other x-coordinate.
questions.hint_html: Substitute y, expand, and retain the zero root.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: check 3
questions.prompt_html: How many intersections do \(y=x+1\) and \(y=x^2+2\) have?
questions.hint_html: Use the discriminant after eliminating y.

questions.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The line \(y=4x+k\) is tangent to \(y=x^2\). Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Tangency gives a repeated root.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: check 1
questions.hint_html: Solve f(x)=9.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the inverse of \(f(x)=3-2x\).
questions.hint_html: Swap input and output, then solve for the new output.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: check 3
questions.hint_html: Solve (x+1)/(x-2)=3, respecting the denominator.

questions.title: Inverse functions, domain and range: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which function is one-to-one on the whole real line?
questions.hint_html: A horizontal line must not meet the graph twice.
questions.solution_html: \(x^3+2\) is strictly increasing; the other functions repeat output values.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: check 1
questions.hint_html: Apply the inside function first.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: check 2
questions.hint_html: Reverse the order carefully.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Let \(f(x)=\sqrt{x}\), \(g(x)=x-4\). What is the real domain of \(f(g(x))\)?
questions.hint_html: The argument of a real square root must be non-negative.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Let \(f:A\to B\) and \(g\) have domain \(C\). When can \(g\circ f\) use every input of \(f\)?
options: When C is contained in A
When the range of f is contained in C
When the domain of f equals the range of g
questions.hint_html: Every output of the inner function must be an allowed input of the outer one.
questions.solution_html: The range of f must lie in the domain of g. Otherwise some proposed composite inputs are invalid.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: check 1
questions.hint_html: The domain selects one square-root branch.
questions.solution_html: Original inputs satisfy \(x-3\ge0\), so the inverse uses the positive square root.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: check 2
questions.hint_html: The original input must lie on the left branch.

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: check 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=(x-3)^2+2\), \(x\ge3\), enter the lower endpoint of the range.
questions.hint_html: Find the minimum of the square.
questions.solution_html: The square is at least zero and is zero at \(x=3\). The range is \([2,\infty)\).

questions.title: Restricting a quadratic to obtain an inverse: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Why does \(f(x)=x^2\) have no inverse function on all real inputs?
options: Both x and -x give the same output
questions.hint_html: An inverse function needs a unique original input.
questions.solution_html: For example, f(2)=f(-2)=4. Without a domain restriction, the inverse of 4 would not be unique.

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: check 1
questions.prompt_html: The graph of \(f\) contains \((2,7)\). Enter the x-coordinate of the corresponding point on \(f^{-1}\).
questions.hint_html: Swap the coordinates.
questions.solution_html: The inverse graph contains \((7,2)\), so its x-coordinate is \(7\).

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: check 2
questions.prompt_html: The graphs of a one-to-one function and its inverse are reflections in which line?
questions.hint_html: Inversion swaps horizontal and vertical coordinates.

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: check 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=3x-8\), find the x-coordinate where its graph crosses \(y=x\).
questions.hint_html: At a fixed point, f(x)=x.
questions.solution_html: \(3x-8=x\), hence \(x=4\); the point \((4,4)\) lies on both graphs.

questions.title: A function and its inverse on a graph: check 4
questions.prompt_html: If the range of a one-to-one function is \([5,\infty)\), what is the domain of its inverse?
questions.hint_html: The inverse takes the original outputs as its inputs.
questions.solution_html: Domain and range exchange under inversion, retaining the endpoint.

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Point \((3,5)\) is on \(y=f(x)\). Find the x-coordinate of its image on \(y=f(x-4)\).
questions.hint_html: An inside shift has the opposite sign.
questions.solution_html: The graph moves right 4, so \((3,5)\) becomes \((7,5)\).

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Point \((3,5)\) is on \(y=f(x)\). Find the y-coordinate of its image on \(y=-2f(x)+1\).
questions.hint_html: Apply the outside operations to the output.

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Which describes \(y=f(3x)\) relative to \(y=f(x)\)?
questions.hint_html: To retain an old input a, solve 3x=a.
questions.solution_html: Each x-coordinate is divided by 3: a horizontal scale factor of 1/3.

questions.title: Transformations, stretches and coordinate rules: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Point \((2,-3)\) is on \(y=f(x)\). For \(y=2f(x+1)-4\), enter the y-coordinate of its image.
questions.hint_html: The inside operation changes x; the outside operations change y.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the distance between \((-2,1)\) and \((4,9)\).
questions.hint_html: Use the right triangle formed by the coordinate differences.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the y-coordinate of the midpoint of \((-5,8)\) and \((7,-2)\).
questions.hint_html: Average the two y-coordinates.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: check 3
questions.prompt_html: \(M=(2,-1)\) is the midpoint of \(A=(-3,4)\) and \(B\). Find the x-coordinate of \(B\).
questions.hint_html: Twice the midpoint equals the sum of the endpoints.

questions.title: Distance, midpoint and geometric reasoning: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which point is equidistant from \((0,0)\) and \((6,0)\)?
questions.hint_html: The perpendicular bisector is vertical.
questions.solution_html: The perpendicular bisector is \(x=3\). Only \((3,5)\) lies on it.

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of a line perpendicular to \(y=4x-3\).
questions.hint_html: The gradients of non-vertical perpendicular lines multiply to -1.

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A line parallel to \(2x-5y=7\) has gradient \(m\). Find \(m\).
questions.hint_html: Rearrange to y=mx+c.

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A line perpendicular to \(x=6\) passes through \((2,-4)\). What is its equation?
questions.hint_html: A vertical line is perpendicular to a horizontal line.
questions.solution_html: The required horizontal line through the point is \(y=-4\).

questions.title: Parallel, perpendicular and exceptional lines: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The line \(y=mx+8\) is perpendicular to the line through \((1,2)\) and \((4,8)\). Find \(m\).
questions.hint_html: First calculate the given line gradient.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A line has gradient 3 and passes through \((2,-1)\). Find its y-intercept.
questions.hint_html: Substitute the point into y=3x+c.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of the line through \((-1,4)\) and \((3,-8)\).
questions.hint_html: Divide the change in y by the change in x.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the x-coordinate of the intersection of \(y=2x+5\) and \(y=-x-1\).
questions.hint_html: Equate the two y-expressions.

questions.title: Straight-line equations, intercepts and intersections: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which is the equation of the vertical line through \((-3,7)\)?
questions.hint_html: All points on a vertical line have the same x-coordinate.
questions.solution_html: The x-coordinate is constantly \(-3\); its gradient is undefined.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the radius of \((x-4)^2+(y+2)^2=49\).
questions.hint_html: The right side is the radius squared.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the x-coordinate of the centre of \(x^2+y^2-6x+8y=0\).
questions.hint_html: Complete the squares.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A circle has diameter endpoints \((-2,1)\), \((4,9)\). Find its radius.
questions.hint_html: Its diameter is the distance between the endpoints.
questions.solution_html: The diameter is \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\), so the radius is \(5\).

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The circle \(x^2+y^2=25\) has tangent at \((3,4)\). Which equation is that tangent?
questions.hint_html: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius and passes through (3,4).
questions.solution_html: The radius gradient is \(4/3\), so the tangent gradient is \(-3/4\): \(3x+4y=25\).

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: check 1
questions.prompt_html: How many intersections do \(y=3\) and \(x^2+y^2=25\) have?
questions.hint_html: Substitute the line into the circle.

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the length of the chord cut by \(y=3\) on \(x^2+y^2=25\).
questions.hint_html: Find both intersection points.
questions.solution_html: The endpoints are \((-4,3)\), \((4,3)\); the chord length is \(8\).

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: check 3
questions.prompt_html: How does \(y=6\) meet \(x^2+y^2=25\)?
questions.hint_html: Compare the line distance from the centre with the radius.
questions.solution_html: The distance \(6\) exceeds the radius \(5\), so the line misses the circle.

questions.title: Line–circle intersections, chords and tangency: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The line \(y=k\), with \(k>0\), is tangent to \(x^2+y^2=36\). Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Tangency occurs one radius from the centre.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Write \(150^\circ=k\pi\) radians. Enter \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Use 180 degrees = pi radians.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Convert \(7\pi/6\) radians to degrees.
questions.hint_html: Multiply by 180/pi.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: check 3
questions.prompt_html: An arc has length 9 cm on a circle of radius 6 cm. Find its angle in radians.
questions.hint_html: Use angle = arc length / radius.

questions.title: Radians, degrees and complete rotations: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which formula for arc length is valid when \(\theta\) is in radians?
questions.hint_html: One radian subtends an arc of one radius.
questions.solution_html: For radian measure, \(s=r\theta\). Degree values must first be converted.

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the arc length in cm for radius 8 cm and angle 1.25 radians.
questions.hint_html: Multiply radius by radian angle.

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A sector has arc length 12 cm and radius 5 cm. Find its perimeter in cm.
questions.hint_html: Include the two straight radii.

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A circle has radius 7 cm. Its minor arc subtends 2 radians. The major arc has length \((14\pi-k)\) cm. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Subtract the minor arc from the circumference.
questions.solution_html: The minor arc is \(7(2)=14\) cm; the major arc is \(14\pi-14\).

questions.title: Arc length, sector perimeter and rolling distance: check 4
questions.prompt_html: For a fixed radius, doubling the angle of a sector does what to its arc length?
questions.hint_html: Arc length is proportional to the radian angle.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the sector area in square cm for \(r=6\) cm, \(\theta=1.5\) radians.
questions.hint_html: Use half r squared times theta.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A sector of radius 4 cm has area 12 square cm. Find its angle in radians.
questions.hint_html: Rearrange the area formula.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A sector has area 30 square cm and arc length 10 cm. Find its radius in cm.
questions.hint_html: Eliminate theta using s = r theta.

questions.title: Sector area and a fixed-perimeter constraint: check 4
questions.prompt_html: At a fixed angle, tripling the radius multiplies the sector area by what factor?
questions.hint_html: Area depends on the square of the radius.

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: check 1
questions.prompt_html: For radius \(r\) and minor angle \(0<\theta<\pi\) in radians, which is the minor segment area?
questions.hint_html: Remove the triangle from the sector.
questions.solution_html: Sector area minus triangle area is \(\tfrac12r^2\theta-\tfrac12r^2\sin\theta\).

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A radius-4 cm circle has a minor sector angle \(\pi/2\). The minor segment area is \((4\pi-k)\) square cm. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: The triangle has two perpendicular radii.
questions.solution_html: The sector area is \(4\pi\), and triangle area is \(\tfrac12(4)(4)=8\).

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A chord subtends \(\pi/3\) at the centre of a radius-9 cm circle. Find the chord length in cm.
questions.hint_html: Use two radii and the included angle.
questions.solution_html: The triangle is equilateral, so the chord length equals the radius, \(9\) cm.

questions.title: Chords, minor segments and major segments: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The minor segment has area \(S\) in a circle of radius \(r\). What is the major segment area?
questions.hint_html: The two segments together form the whole disk.
questions.solution_html: The disk area is \(\pi r^2\); subtract \(S\).

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: check 1
questions.prompt_html: An annular sector has outer radius 7 cm, inner radius 3 cm, angle 0.8 radians. Find its area in square cm.
questions.hint_html: Subtract the inner sector area from the outer sector area.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: check 2
questions.prompt_html: An annular sector has radii 7 cm and 3 cm, angle 0.8 radians. Find its complete perimeter in cm.
questions.hint_html: Include two arcs and two radial edges.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Two non-overlapping sectors of the same circle have angles 0.6 and 0.9 radians. If the radius is 4 cm, find their total area in square cm.
questions.hint_html: Add the angles before applying the area formula.

questions.title: Annular sectors and composite boundaries: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Two equal sectors overlap in a region of area \(B\). Each sector has area \(A\). What is their union area?
questions.hint_html: The overlap was counted twice when adding the areas.

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find \(\cos120^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Use the reference angle 60 degrees and the quadrant sign.

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find \(\tan225^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Tangent repeats every 180 degrees.

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: check 3
questions.prompt_html: If \(\sin\theta=3/5\) and \(90^\circ<\theta<180^\circ\), find \(\cos\theta\).
questions.hint_html: Use the identity, then choose the quadrant sign.
questions.solution_html: \(\cos^2\theta=1-9/25=16/25\); cosine is negative in quadrant II.

questions.title: Exact values, quadrants and general angles: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which equals \(\sin(5\pi/3)\)?
questions.hint_html: The angle is 300 degrees, in quadrant IV.
questions.solution_html: Its reference angle is \(\pi/3\), and sine is negative: \(-\sqrt3/2\).

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the amplitude of \(y=5-3\sin(2x)\).
questions.hint_html: Amplitude is the absolute outside multiplier.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=\cos(4x)\), the period is \(k\pi\) radians. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Divide 2 pi by the inside multiplier.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the maximum value of \(y=2+4\cos x\).
questions.hint_html: Cosine has maximum 1.

questions.title: Trigonometric graphs, periods and transformations: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Where are the vertical asymptotes of \(y=\tan x\) on \(0\le x\le2\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Tangent is undefined where cosine is zero.
questions.solution_html: Within the interval, \(\cos x=0\) at \(\pi/2\) and \(3\pi/2\).

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Where \(\cos x\ne0\), simplify \(\sin x/\cos x\).
questions.hint_html: Recall the quotient identity.
questions.solution_html: By definition, \(\tan x=\sin x/\cos x\), with the stated restriction.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\cos x=0.6\), find \(\sin^2x\).
questions.hint_html: Use sine squared plus cosine squared = 1.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: check 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(\sin x\ne0\), simplify \(\frac{1-\cos^2x}{\sin x}\).
questions.hint_html: Replace the numerator using the Pythagorean identity.
questions.solution_html: \((1-\cos^2x)/\sin x=\sin^2x/\sin x=\sin x\) on the stated domain.

questions.title: Identities, factorisation and valid domains: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which statement is an identity wherever both sides are defined?
questions.hint_html: An identity holds for every input in its domain.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\sin x=1/2\) for \(0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the principal value of \(\sin^{-1}(1/2)\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Use the principal inverse-sine range.
questions.solution_html: The principal range is \([-90^\circ,90^\circ]\), so the answer is \(30^\circ\).

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\cos(2x)=0\) on \(0\le x\le\pi\).
questions.hint_html: Double the entire interval before solving.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: check 4
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\sin x=0\) have in \(0\le x\le2\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Check both interval endpoints.
questions.solution_html: The roots are \(0,\pi,2\pi\), so there are three.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(2\sin^2x-\sin x-1=0\) on \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Factor as a quadratic in sin x.
questions.solution_html: \((2\sin x+1)(\sin x-1)=0\); sine is \(-1/2\) or \(1\), giving the three listed roots.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: check 2
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\cos^2x-3\cos x+2=0\) have for \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.hint_html: Reject impossible cosine values.
questions.solution_html: \((\cos x-1)(\cos x-2)=0\). Only \(\cos x=1\) is possible, giving \(x=0\).

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\sin x\cos x=0\) on \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Do not divide by a factor which can be zero.
questions.solution_html: Either sine or cosine is zero, so all four multiples of \(90^\circ\) in the interval occur.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: check 4
questions.prompt_html: How many roots does \(\tan^2x=1\) have on \(-\pi/2<x<\pi/2\)?
questions.hint_html: Take both signs, excluding undefined endpoints.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: check 1
questions.prompt_html: An AP has first term 7 and common difference -3. Find its eighth term.
questions.hint_html: Use a+(n-1)d.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum of the first 12 terms of the AP \(4,9,14,\ldots\).
questions.hint_html: Find the last term, then average first and last.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: check 3
questions.prompt_html: The third and seventh terms of an AP are 11 and 27. Find its common difference.
questions.hint_html: Four term steps account for the difference 16.

questions.title: Arithmetic progressions: terms, sums and integer thresholds: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The numbers \(k,11,19\) are consecutive terms of an AP. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: The middle term is the average of its neighbours.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A GP has first term 3 and common ratio 2. Find its sixth term.
questions.hint_html: Use a r to the power n-1.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum of the first four terms of \(5,15,45,\ldots\).
questions.hint_html: Add the four terms or use the finite sum formula.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the sum to infinity of \(12,-6,3,\ldots\).
questions.hint_html: The ratio is negative and has magnitude less than 1.

questions.title: Geometric progressions: finite sums and convergence: check 4
questions.prompt_html: For which ratio does a nonzero GP have a finite sum to infinity?
questions.hint_html: The magnitude, not just the sign, matters.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Three angles \(20^\circ,\theta,80^\circ\) are in AP. Find \(\theta\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: The middle term is their arithmetic mean.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Angles form the AP \(15^\circ,25^\circ,35^\circ,\ldots\). Find the ninth angle in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Use a=15 and d=10.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: check 3
questions.prompt_html: If angles form an AP, must their sine values also form an AP?
options: Only if the common difference is positive
No, sine is not a linear function
questions.hint_html: Test angles 0, 30 and 60 degrees.
questions.solution_html: The angles are in AP, but their sines \(0,1/2,\sqrt3/2\) have unequal successive differences.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in an arithmetic progression: check 4
questions.prompt_html: \(\sin30^\circ,k,\sin90^\circ\) are consecutive AP terms. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Average the two known sine values.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Angles \(10^\circ,30^\circ,\theta\) are consecutive GP terms. Find \(\theta\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: The common ratio is 3.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: check 2
questions.prompt_html: \(\cos60^\circ,k,\cos0^\circ\) form a GP with \(k>0\). Find \(k^2\).
questions.hint_html: For three consecutive GP terms, the middle squared is the product of its neighbours.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A GP has first term \(\sin30^\circ\) and ratio \(\cos60^\circ\). Find its sum to infinity.
questions.hint_html: Both known trig values equal one half.

questions.title: Trigonometric terms in a geometric progression: check 4
questions.prompt_html: For a GP with ratio \(\tan\theta\), \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), when does its nonzero infinite sum converge?
questions.hint_html: On this interval tangent increases from zero.

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A display has 8 tiles in its first row and 3 more in each subsequent row. How many tiles are in its first 10 rows?
questions.hint_html: This is an arithmetic sum.
questions.solution_html: The tenth row has \(8+9(3)=35\) tiles. The total is \(10(8+35)/2=215\).

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A culture triples every hour and initially contains 20 units. How many units are there after 4 hours?
questions.hint_html: The initial amount is at time zero.
questions.solution_html: The amount after four multiplications is \(20(3^4)=1620\).

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A machine releases 16 g in its first pulse and half as much in every later pulse. Find the total mass in grams over infinitely many pulses.
questions.hint_html: Use a convergent geometric sum.

questions.title: Series models: accumulation, decay and repeated motion: check 4
questions.prompt_html: A savings total starts at 100 and gains a fixed 12 each month, with no interest. Which sequence models the totals?
questions.hint_html: A fixed additive change is not a fixed proportional change.
questions.solution_html: Each new total exceeds the previous one by 12, so the totals form an AP.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((1+2x)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Choose two factors contributing 2x.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x\) in \((3-x)^3\).
questions.hint_html: Select one -x and two constant factors.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the constant term in \((2+x)^5\).
questions.hint_html: Choose the constant from every factor.

questions.title: Finite binomial expansions and signs: check 4
questions.prompt_html: How many nonzero terms occur in the fully expanded \((1+x)^6\)?
questions.hint_html: Powers range from zero through six.
questions.solution_html: There is one term for each power \(x^0\) to \(x^6\), seven terms.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^3\) in \((1+x)^7\).
questions.hint_html: Use the binomial coefficient 7 choose 3.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: check 2
questions.prompt_html: In \((2+x)^5\), find the coefficient of \(x^4\).
questions.hint_html: Four x factors leave one constant factor.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the constant term in \((x^2+2/x)^3\), \(x\ne0\).
questions.hint_html: If r factors contribute 2/x, the power is 6-3r.

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which is the term containing \(x^r\) in \((a+bx)^n\), with integer \(0\le r\le n\)?
questions.hint_html: Choose r factors supplying bx.
questions.solution_html: There are \(\binom nr\) choices, each contributing \(a^{n-r}(bx)^r\).

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((1+x)(1+2x)^3\).
questions.hint_html: Include both ways the total power can be 2.
questions.solution_html: The contributions are \(12x^2\) and \(x(6x)\), giving coefficient \(18\).

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x\) in \((2-x)(1+3x)^2\).
questions.hint_html: Combine constant times linear and linear times constant.

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the coefficient of \(x^3\) in \((1-x)(1+x)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Use the x cubed and x squared terms from the second factor.

questions.title: Coefficients in products and parity: check 4
questions.prompt_html: To find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in a product, which pairs of powers must be considered?
questions.hint_html: The two exponents must add to 2.
questions.solution_html: The possible non-negative exponent pairs are precisely \((0,2),(1,1),(2,0)\).

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: check 1
questions.prompt_html: The coefficient of \(x\) in \((1+kx)^5\) is 20. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: The linear coefficient is 5k.

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: check 2
questions.prompt_html: In \((1+kx)^4\), \(k>0\), the coefficient of \(x^2\) is 54. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: The coefficient is 6k squared.

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: check 3
questions.prompt_html: In \((2+kx)^3\), the coefficient of \(x\) is -24. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Remember the two constant factors each equal 2.

questions.title: Unknown constants and an unknown exponent: check 4
questions.prompt_html: In \((1+kx)^4\), the coefficient of \(x^2\) is 24, with no sign restriction on \(k\). What are the possible values?
questions.hint_html: A squared parameter can have two signs.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Use terms through \(x^2\) in \((1+x)^5\) to approximate \((1.02)^5\). Enter the approximation.
questions.hint_html: Substitute x=0.02 after truncating.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Use \(1-4x+6x^2\) to approximate \((0.97)^4\).
questions.hint_html: Here x=0.03.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: check 3
questions.prompt_html: For small positive \(x\), does \(1+4x+6x^2\) overestimate or underestimate \((1+x)^4\)?
questions.hint_html: Inspect the omitted terms.
questions.solution_html: The omitted \(4x^3+x^4\) is positive, so the truncated expression underestimates.

questions.title: Finite expansions as approximations: keep the remainder: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Why is the expansion of \((1+x)^5\) a finite polynomial?
options: Because the exponent is a non-negative integer
Because only three terms are permitted
questions.hint_html: Distinguish a finite binomial expansion from an infinite series.
questions.solution_html: There are five factors; no power above \(x^5\) can occur. No convergence restriction on x is needed.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: check 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^3-4x\), find \(dy/dx\) at \(x=2\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate term by term.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=\sqrt{x}+x^{-1}\), find \(dy/dx\) at \(x=4\).
questions.hint_html: Write the root as x to the power one half.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: check 3
questions.hint_html: Include the derivative of the inner linear function.

questions.title: Derivatives: powers, linear inner functions and domains: check 4
questions.prompt_html: On \(y=x^2\), the chord from \(x=3\) to \(x=3+h\) has gradient \(6+h\). What value does this approach as \(h\to0\)?
questions.hint_html: Let the second point approach the first.

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of the tangent to \(y=x^2+1\) at \(x=3\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate and evaluate.

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of the normal to \(y=x^2+1\) at \(x=3\).
questions.hint_html: Take the negative reciprocal of the tangent gradient.
questions.solution_html: The tangent gradient is \(6\); the normal gradient is \(-1/6\).

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: check 3
questions.prompt_html: The tangent to \(y=x^2\) at \(x=2\) has equation \(y=4x+c\). Find \(c\).
questions.hint_html: The tangent passes through (2,4).

questions.title: Tangents, normals and the zero-gradient case: check 4
questions.prompt_html: What is the normal to \(y=x^2\) at its vertex?
questions.hint_html: The tangent at the vertex is horizontal.
questions.solution_html: The perpendicular normal is vertical, with equation \(x=0\).

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: check 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^3-3x\), find \(y\prime\prime\) at \(x=1\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate twice.

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^3-3x\), what is the nature of the stationary point at \(x=1\)?
options: Cannot decide from the second derivative
questions.hint_html: Check both first and second derivatives there.
questions.solution_html: \(y\prime(1)=0\), \(y\prime\prime(1)=6>0\), so it is a local minimum.

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Where is \(y=x^2-6x+2\) strictly decreasing?
questions.hint_html: A negative first derivative indicates decrease.

questions.title: Increasing, decreasing and stationary points: check 4
questions.prompt_html: At a stationary point, \(f\prime\prime(a)=0\). What follows from this second-derivative test alone?
options: It is never a turning point
questions.hint_html: Zero second derivative does not classify the point.
questions.solution_html: Further analysis, such as the sign change of \(f\prime\), is needed. A zero second derivative alone proves neither maximum nor minimum.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Let \(y=x^2\) and \(dx/dt=3\). Find \(dy/dt\) when \(x=4\).
questions.hint_html: Multiply dy/dx by dx/dt.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A square side \(s\) grows at 0.5 cm/s. Find the area growth rate in square cm/s when \(s=6\) cm.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate A=s squared with respect to time.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: check 3
questions.prompt_html: The radius of a sphere grows at 0.2 cm/s. When \(r=5\) cm, \(dV/dt=k\pi\) cubic cm/s. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Use V=4 pi r cubed /3 and the chain rule.

questions.title: Related rates and small increments: check 4
questions.prompt_html: A length decreases at 2 cm/s. Which represents its signed rate?
questions.hint_html: A decreasing quantity has a negative derivative.
questions.solution_html: The signed rate is \(-2\) cm/s; the length itself need not be negative.

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A rectangle has perimeter 24 cm. Find the width in cm giving the greatest area.
questions.hint_html: Write area as w(12-w).

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum of \(f(x)=x+16/x\) for \(x>0\).
questions.hint_html: Find the positive stationary point.
questions.solution_html: \(f\prime=1-16/x^2=0\) gives \(x=4\). The derivative changes from negative to positive; \(f(4)=8\).

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the maximum of \(f(x)=x^2\) on \([-1,3]\).
questions.hint_html: Compare stationary points and endpoints.
questions.solution_html: The candidates are \(x=-1,0,3\), with values \(1,0,9\). The maximum is \(9\).

questions.title: Optimisation on a feasible domain: check 4
questions.prompt_html: After finding a stationary point in an optimisation problem, what must also be checked?
options: Only whether x is an integer
Feasibility, nature and any relevant boundaries
Only whether the derivative exists at zero
questions.hint_html: A stationary point may be outside the allowed domain or may be a minimum.
questions.solution_html: Check the model domain, classify the point and compare relevant boundary values to justify the requested optimum.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: check 1
questions.prompt_html: An antiderivative of \(6x^2\) is \(ax^3+C\). Find \(a\).
questions.hint_html: Increase the power and divide by the new power.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: check 2
questions.prompt_html: An antiderivative of \((2x+1)^3\) is \(a(2x+1)^4+C\). Find \(a\).
questions.hint_html: Account for both the new exponent and the inner derivative.
questions.solution_html: Differentiating the proposed form gives \(8a(2x+1)^3\), so \(a=1/8\).

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the improper integral \(\int_0^1 x^{-1/2}\,dx\).
questions.hint_html: Use an antiderivative and a right-hand limit at zero.
questions.solution_html: \(\lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}[2\sqrt{x}]_\varepsilon^1=2\). The singular integrand has a finite integral.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: check 4
questions.prompt_html: For which power does \(\int x^n\,dx=x^{n+1}/(n+1)+C\) fail?
questions.hint_html: The denominator n+1 must be nonzero.
questions.solution_html: The displayed power rule excludes \(n=-1\). This short course does not use it for that exponent.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A curve has \(dy/dx=4x-3\) and passes through \((2,5)\). Write \(y=2x^2-3x+C\) and find \(C\).
questions.hint_html: Substitute the given point after integrating.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A curve has \(dy/dx=3x^2\), \(y(1)=4\). Find \(y(2)\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate, then use the initial value.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Given \(y\prime\prime=6x\) and \(y\prime(0)=2\), find \(y\prime(1)\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate the second derivative once.

questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Why must \(+C\) be included in an indefinite integral?
options: Every curve passes through the origin
Functions differing by a constant have the same derivative
It changes the derivative by C
questions.hint_html: Differentiating a constant gives zero.
questions.solution_html: The derivative does not determine the vertical translation. An initial condition can determine C.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Find the area under \(y=3x^2\) above the x-axis from \(x=0\) to \(x=2\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate over the given bounds.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: check 2
questions.prompt_html: Find the total geometric area between \(y=x\) and the x-axis from \(x=-1\) to \(x=1\).
questions.hint_html: Split where the graph crosses the axis.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the area between \(y=2x\) and \(y=x^2\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=2\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate upper curve minus lower curve.

questions.title: Signed integrals and geometric areas: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Find the area between \(y=4\) and \(y=x^2\) for \(-2\le x\le2\).
questions.hint_html: The line is above the curve on this interval.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: check 1
questions.prompt_html: The region under \(y=x\), \(0\le x\le3\), rotates about the x-axis. Its volume is \(k\pi\). Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate y squared with respect to x.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: check 2
questions.prompt_html: The region between \(x=y^2\) and the y-axis, \(0\le y\le2\), rotates about the y-axis. Find \(V/\pi\).
questions.hint_html: Use horizontal disks, with radius x=y squared.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: check 3
questions.prompt_html: The region \(1\le y\le2\), \(0\le x\le3\), rotates about the x-axis. Find \(V/\pi\).
questions.hint_html: Use the difference of squared radii.

questions.title: Volumes of revolution: disks and washers: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Which is the correct washer integrand for outer radius \(R\) and inner radius \(r\)?
questions.hint_html: Subtract areas of disks, not radii before squaring.
questions.solution_html: The cross-sectional area is \(\pi R^2-\pi r^2\).

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A flow rate is \(q(t)=2t+3\) litres/minute. How many litres enter from \(t=0\) to \(t=4\) minutes?
questions.hint_html: Integrate the rate over the time interval.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: check 2
questions.prompt_html: An amount starts at 10 units and has rate \(dQ/dt=6t\). Find \(Q(3)\).
questions.hint_html: Add the accumulated change to the initial amount.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A quantity has signed rate \(2t-4\) from \(t=0\) to \(t=4\). Find its net change.
questions.hint_html: Integrate the signed rate; do not take absolute values.
questions.solution_html: \(\Delta Q=[t^2-4t]_0^4=0\); equal losses and gains cancel.

questions.title: Accumulation and mixed calculus review: check 4
questions.prompt_html: A quantity has rate \(2t-4\) from \(t=0\) to \(t=4\). Find the total variation, the integral of the absolute rate.
questions.hint_html: Split the integral at t=2.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: check 1
questions.prompt_html: Let \(f(x)=x^2-6x+13\), \(x\ge3\). Find the lower endpoint of the domain of \(f^{-1}\).
questions.hint_html: Complete the square to find the range of f.
questions.solution_html: \(f(x)=(x-3)^2+4\). Its range, hence inverse domain, is \([4,\infty)\).

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: check 2
questions.hint_html: Choose the original allowed branch.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: check 3
questions.hint_html: Apply g first and square its full output.
questions.solution_html: \(f(g(x))=f(x-5)=(x-5)^2\), a horizontal translation of the quadratic.

questions.title: Quadratics, functions and admissible solutions: check 4
questions.prompt_html: For \(f(x)=(x-2)^2+3\), which \(k\) gives two distinct solutions of \(f(x)=k\) over all real x?
questions.hint_html: Compare the horizontal line with the vertex.
questions.solution_html: \((x-2)^2=k-3\) has two distinct real roots exactly when \(k-3>0\).

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: check 1
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=x^2+2x\), find the tangent gradient at \(x=1\).
questions.hint_html: Use the derivative before constructing the line.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: check 2
questions.prompt_html: The tangent in the preceding setting passes through \((1,3)\). Its equation is \(y=4x+c\). Find \(c\).
questions.hint_html: Use the given point to fix the intercept.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: check 3
questions.prompt_html: Find the gradient of the tangent to \(x^2+y^2=25\) at \((3,4)\), using radius geometry.
questions.hint_html: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
questions.solution_html: The radius has gradient \(4/3\), so the tangent gradient is \(-3/4\). No implicit differentiation is needed.

questions.title: Lines, circles and derivatives: check 4
questions.prompt_html: The normal to \(y=x^2\) at \((1,1)\) meets the y-axis at \((0,b)\). Find \(b\).
questions.hint_html: Use normal gradient -1/2 and point (1,1).

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A sector has radius 6 cm and angle \(\pi/3\). Its arc length is \(k\pi\) cm. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Use the radian angle directly.

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: check 2
questions.prompt_html: For radius 6 cm and angle \(\pi/3\), the minor segment area is \(6\pi-k\sqrt3\) square cm. Find \(k\).
questions.hint_html: Subtract the triangle using exact sine.
questions.solution_html: The triangle area is \(18\sin(\pi/3)=9\sqrt3\), while the sector area is \(6\pi\).

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: check 3
questions.prompt_html: A sector angle is \(120^\circ\). Which radian value belongs in \(A=\tfrac12r^2\theta\)?
questions.hint_html: Multiply the degree measure by pi/180.

questions.title: Trigonometric branches and sector models: check 4
questions.prompt_html: A chord of a radius-8 cm circle subtends \(\pi/3\). Find its length in cm.
questions.hint_html: Use the isosceles triangle or chord formula.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: check 1
questions.prompt_html: An AP has \(u_n=3n+2\). Find the coefficient of \(x\) in \((1+x)^{u_2}\).
questions.hint_html: First evaluate the positive integer exponent.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: check 2
questions.prompt_html: A GP begins \(2,6,18,\ldots\). Its third term is \(a\). Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((1+ax)^3\).
questions.hint_html: Find a, then use the binomial coefficient.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: check 3
questions.prompt_html: The coefficients of \(1,x,x^2\) in \((1+x)^4\) form a short sequence. Find their sum.
questions.hint_html: Read the first three binomial coefficients.

questions.title: Coefficients as sequence data: check 4
questions.prompt_html: Are the first three coefficients \(1,4,6\) of \((1+x)^4\) an AP or GP?
questions.hint_html: Check both successive differences and ratios.
questions.solution_html: The differences are 3 and 2, while the ratios are 4 and 1.5; neither is constant.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: check 1
questions.prompt_html: A model has \(Q(t)=t^3-3t^2+12\). Find its instantaneous rate at \(t=3\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate the amount, not its average.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: check 2
questions.prompt_html: The signed rate is \(q(t)=3t^2-6t\). Find the net change from \(t=0\) to \(t=3\).
questions.hint_html: Integrate the signed rate.

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: check 3
questions.prompt_html: For \(Q(t)=t^3-3t^2+12\), find the minimum value on \(0\le t\le3\).
questions.hint_html: Compare the endpoints with stationary t=2.
questions.solution_html: The values at \(t=0,2,3\) are \(12,8,12\), so the minimum is \(8\).

questions.title: Recovered curves, regions and accumulated quantities: check 4
questions.prompt_html: A rate is measured in litres per second and integrated with respect to time in seconds. What units does the integral have?
questions.hint_html: Multiply the rate units by the time units.
questions.solution_html: (Litres/second) times seconds gives litres, an accumulated amount.

questions.title: The discriminant and parameter conditions: check 5
questions.prompt_html: Use the quadratic formula for \(2x^2-3x-1=0\). Which is its complete solution?
questions.hint_html: Use a=2, b=-3, c=-1 and denominator 2a.

questions.title: Composite functions and their domains: check 5
questions.prompt_html: Let \(f(x)=1/x\), \(x\ge2\). What is its range?
questions.hint_html: The value at 2 is attained; zero is only approached.
questions.solution_html: For finite \(x\ge2\), \(0<1/x\le1/2\). Every value in this interval occurs.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: check 5
questions.prompt_html: Find the principal value of \(\cos^{-1}(-1/2)\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: Principal inverse cosine takes values from 0 to 180 degrees.

questions.title: Trigonometric equations on a stated interval: check 6
questions.prompt_html: Find the principal value of \(\tan^{-1}(-1)\) in degrees.
questions.hint_html: The principal inverse-tangent range is between -90 and 90 degrees.
questions.solution_html: The value is \(-45^\circ\), not \(135^\circ\), because the principal range is \((-90^\circ,90^\circ)\).

questions.title: Trigonometric equations that become quadratics: check 5
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\sqrt3\sin x=\cos x\) on \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: Check the cosine-zero cases before dividing.
questions.solution_html: When \(\cos x=0\), the original equation fails. Otherwise \(\tan x=1/\sqrt3\), giving \(30^\circ,210^\circ\).

questions.title: The general term and powers of x: check 5
questions.prompt_html: Evaluate \(\frac{6!}{2!4!}\).
questions.hint_html: Cancel 4 factorial before multiplying.

questions.title: Circle equations and tangents: check 5
questions.prompt_html: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a different point on that circle. What is angle ACB?
questions.hint_html: Use the angle-in-a-semicircle property.
questions.solution_html: An angle subtended by a diameter at any other point of the circle is a right angle.

questions.title: Power integrals, constants and limits: check 5
questions.prompt_html: For \(x>-1/3\), an antiderivative of \((3x+1)^{-2}\) is \(a(3x+1)^{-1}+C\). Find \(a\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate the proposed form, including the inner derivative.
questions.focus: negative power with linear inner function
